oldScript.headline: Two hellos we refuse.
oldScript.goodbyeBody: Boxes in the landing. The patio does not fit in the flat. You close the window and tell yourself that’s that.
oldScript.helloBody: The phone face-down. The building chat. Nobody is shouting in this picture. Fear is enough.

object.headline: The object.
object.body: An extractor for the balcony grill. It captures smoke at the grate — charcoal included. Facts, not theatre.
object.cleanAlt: Lume’s tray and filter in the sink.

domingo.headline: Asado Sunday. Here too.
domingo.body: Table, hands, late light. The window next door stays open. The building is still a building.
domingo.civicAlt: Night balcony: someone is cooking and the neighbour’s window is open.
domingo.goldenAlt: Golden-hour asado on a balcony, table set, charcoal lit.

building.headline: A courtesy, not a permit.
building.quote: Lume does not legalise fire. It makes fire more civil, when fire is allowed.
building.body: The bylaws decide. If charcoal is banned, Lume does not enable it. The note is for the building: what it is, what it does not promise, and that the neighbour stays a neighbour.

privacyPage.metaDescription: Why Lume asks for an email and what we do with it.
privacyPage.title: Why we ask for an email
privacyPage.lead: We want to tell you when Lume is ready for the first Sunday. That is all.
privacyPage.whatBody: The address you leave. If you want, the country, whether you already have a grill, and whether a neighbour sent you. The date you joined. No phone. No street address.
privacyPage.whyBody: To write when the object is ready in Argentina or Spain, and to know which crate to talk about. We do not sell the list. We do not build a profile.
privacyPage.leaveBody: Reply to the notice and ask to be removed. We will.
privacyPage.contact: Questions: hola@lumefuego.com — a person, not a bot.

faqPage.metaDescription: Can you grill on a balcony? What Lume is, what it does not promise, and the note for the building.
faqPage.title: What people usually ask.
faqPage.lead: The bylaws decide. We do not sell miracles or permits. Here, calmly.
faqPage.q1: Can I make asado on the balcony?
faqPage.a1: It depends on your building rules and on not being a problem for the neighbours. Smoke and smell must stay within ordinary tolerance. Lume does not change that rule: it makes fire more civil, when fire is allowed.
faqPage.a2: Lume does not legalise fire. If the building forbids charcoal, the object does not enable it. The note for the building says exactly that, so a chairperson can forward it without surprises.
faqPage.a3: No. That aisle is electric plates. Lume captures smoke at the grate — charcoal included — and reduces the plume and odour leaving the balcony. We do not promise a miracle.
faqPage.q4: Do I have to drill the façade?
faqPage.a4: No. No ducts. No drilling into common structure. It is a household appliance, ordinary plug. The cook stays beside it, talking.
faqPage.q5: Does it work on a real grill?
faqPage.a5: It is built for charcoal. If it only worked on induction, it would not be Lume. Use it over your grill, on the balcony, not as a kitchen rangehood in a closed room.
faqPage.q6: What do I tell the building?
faqPage.a6: Send them the note. It is a courtesy, not a permit: what it is, what it does not promise, and that the neighbour stays a neighbour.
faqPage.a7: Not yet. Leave an email and we will write when the first Sunday is ready in Argentina or Spain.
